checks.name: Administrators use phishing resistant sign in
checks.description: Every account that holds an administrator role must sign in with a phishing resistant factor, such as a security key or a passkey.
checks.remediation: Require a phishing resistant factor for administrator roles, and enrol a security key or passkey for each listed administrator.

controls.rationale: Shows identity provider administrators must use a phishing resistant factor. Cloud root accounts and other systems are checked separately.
Shows privileged identity provider accounts carry stronger sign in protection. Approval and review of those accounts stay with people.

provider_notes.entra: Needs P1: an enabled Conditional Access policy targeting the admin roles with an authentication strength of phishing resistant methods only (FIDO2, Windows Hello for Business, certificate based multifactor). Security defaults alone fail; no P1 fails with reason plan. Method value names to confirm.
provider_notes.okta: Whether Okta Verify counts as phishing resistant depends on its configuration (unverified), so those admins read insufficient. The Admin Console policy constraint field name is unverified. Role read may need more than Read-only Administrator.
provider_notes.gws: Uses security key and passkey counts from usage reports, which are 1 to 5 days late, and the 2SV factor policy (PASSKEY_ONLY or a passkey combination). How a policy targets a group is unverified. The policy part errors without a super admin subject.

checks.population: Enabled accounts holding any administrator role (active or eligible) at collection time
checks.predicate: A policy that applies to the account requires a phishing resistant factor, and the account has one enrolled
checks.period: Point in time, daily
checks.empty_population: `error`: an identity provider always has at least one administrator, so an empty list means the role read failed
checks.notes: Fills second-factor-enforcement-and-enrolled-users for IAM-03.C (idp.mfa_enforced fills B, D, E). 1Password is n/a in the matrix. implementations in identity-checks.md say empty until a collector ships; here they follow the brief (supported or partial providers).

checks.name: No unused account stays active
checks.description: No enabled account, member or guest, has gone longer than the allowed period without a successful sign in.
checks.remediation: Disable the listed accounts, or record why each one must stay active.

controls.rationale: Finds accounts nobody uses, which is how missed removals surface. Matching accounts to leavers needs the staff list.
Points reviewers at unused access between reviews. The review and its sign off stay with people.
Finds guest and contractor accounts that outlived their use. The contractor register and end dates stay with people.

evidence_kinds: Account list with last successful sign in

provider_notes.entra: Supported with P1 only: signInActivity needs P1 or P2, so a Free tenant reads error with reason licence. lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime exists only from December 2023; before that use the later of the interactive and non interactive times. A guest still PendingAcceptance counts as inactive. signInActivity reads are limited to 10 a minute.
provider_notes.okta: lastLogin; null means never signed in. Deprovisioned users must be queried explicitly.
provider_notes.gws: The later of lastLoginTime and accounts:timestamp_last_sso.
provider_notes.onepassword: The Users API has no last sign in field.

checks.population: Enabled accounts older than `inactive_days`, members and guests, excluding accounts recorded as exceptions in Verity
checks.predicate: Last successful sign in is within `inactive_days`. An account that never signed in counts as inactive
checks.period: Rolling window of `inactive_days` ending at collection
checks.empty_population: `pass` only when the provider returned a complete user list; otherwise `insufficient information`

parameters.inactive_days: default 90, set from the customer's access policy; accounts created less recently than this are left out

checks.notes: Fills account-list-export for IAM-12.E. Related, not an alias: people.accounts_match_roster (members against the roster; guests are covered here).

checks.name: App credentials have owners and expire
checks.description: Every application or service app that holds a credential in the identity provider has a named owner, and no credential lives longer than the rotation limit.
checks.remediation: Add an owner to the listed applications, and replace credentials that outlive the rotation limit.

controls.rationale: Covers machine identities held in the identity provider. Cloud and build system credentials are checked by `cloud.machine_credentials_rotated`.

provider_notes.entra: App registrations with a secret or certificate: owners and credential start and end dates (never secret values).
provider_notes.okta: Okta apps have no owner field (unverified), so only credential age is judged; API tokens are judged as tied to an active admin. The token listing endpoint and scope are unverified.
provider_notes.gws: Service accounts and delegation clients live in Google Cloud, not the Workspace directory (no Admin SDK listing found, unverified). Covered by cloud.machine_credentials_rotated.

checks.population: Applications registered in the customer's own directory that hold at least one secret or certificate
checks.predicate: At least one owner, and every credential's lifetime (end minus start, or age where no end exists) is at most `max_credential_days`
checks.period: Point in time, daily
checks.empty_population: `pass` with a note when the list was complete (many small tenants have none)

parameters.max_credential_days: default 365, from the customer's access policy

checks.notes: identity.app in 01-evidence-model 1.4 has no owner or credential date fields; extend it with owners and credential dates, or add a new observation type identity.app_credential. records-of-rotation-or-review is filled for IAM-10.D.

checks.name: Identity provider access reviews are finished
checks.description: Every access review that closed in the period has a decision on every item by someone other than the person reviewed, and every removal decided was applied.
checks.remediation: Finish open reviews, reassign self reviews, and apply the removals that were decided.

controls.rationale: Shows reviews run inside the identity provider were completed and acted on. Systems outside it and the review procedure stay with people.
Where privileged roles are reviewed in the identity provider, shows those reviews were completed.

provider_notes.entra: Needs Entra ID Governance, or P2 for features GA in P2, and the optional AccessReview.Read.All permission; without them error with reason licence. Decision field names unverified.
provider_notes.okta: Needs Okta Identity Governance and the optional okta.governance.accessCertifications.read scope; not applicable without it.
provider_notes.gws: Workspace has no access review feature.

checks.population: Review instances that ended in the last 90 days
checks.predicate: No item without a decision; no item decided by the person it is about; every deny decision applied
checks.period: 90 days ending at collection
checks.empty_population: `not_applicable` when the customer runs reviews outside the identity provider (the manual review pack stays the evidence), never `pass`
checks.notes: New observation type proposed: identity.access_review (review instance, decisions, reviewer, principal, apply result); none of the 1.4 types fits. Fills completed-access-reviews-with-reviewer-sign only where the customer reviews inside Entra or Okta.

checks.name: Every account belongs to a current person
checks.description: Every enabled member account in the identity provider matches a person on the current staff and contractor roster, or is a recorded shared or service account with an owner.
checks.remediation: Disable the listed accounts, link each to a person, or record it as a service account with an owner.

controls.rationale: Reconciles accounts with the people who should have them. Systems outside the identity provider need their own reconciliation.
Shows each account maps to one named person. Approval of the access is checked separately.
Shows contractor accounts match the contractor roster. Agreements and training stay with people.

provider_notes.entra: Needs a roster. Match by employee id or UPN.
provider_notes.okta: Needs a roster. Population is users that can sign in.
provider_notes.gws: Needs a roster. Shared or service mailboxes can be recorded as such.

checks.population: Enabled member accounts (guests are covered by `idp.no_inactive_accounts`)
checks.predicate: Matched to an active roster person by immutable id, or by email when the roster has no id, or recorded in Verity as a shared or service account with an owner
checks.period: Point in time, daily
checks.empty_population: `insufficient information` when no roster exists or it is older than its own review period
checks.notes: Fills account-list-export for IAM-12.E and HR-03.B. contractor-register-with-start-and-end is an input, unchanged. hr_system providers are not_planned in capabilities.json; until a roster exists in Verity (continuous compliance plan 6 C proposes a controlled workforce import) it reads insufficient information. Related: idp.no_inactive_accounts, edge.members_current.

checks.name: Leavers lose password manager access
checks.description: No one who left still has an active company password manager account after the allowed time.
checks.remediation: Suspend the listed password manager accounts, and rotate the shared credentials they could read.

controls.rationale: Shows leavers lost vault access. Rotating the shared credentials they could read is recorded by people.
Covers the password manager, one of the systems outside single sign on that removal must reach.

provider_notes.onepassword: Needs a leaver roster. Removal time from the suspend or delete audit event (Events Reporting token, auditevents only), else the first daily snapshot showing the member gone or suspended. The Users API is not available on Teams or when the account uses 1Password automated provisioning; then membership comes from the identity provider's assignment of the 1Password app and the evidence says so.

checks.population: Leavers on the roster whose end date is in the last 90 days
checks.predicate: No active vault account for the leaver later than `removal_hours` after the end date
checks.period: 90 days ending at collection
checks.empty_population: `pass` only when the roster is current and shows no leavers; otherwise `insufficient information`
checks.notes: New observation type proposed: vault.event (password manager audit events: suspend, delete, vault access grant and revoke). Fills removal-records-for-a-sample-of for IAM-12.D and password-manager-members-against-staff-list for IAM-05.B and D (IAM-05.C stays a person). Same predicate shape as people.leavers_deprovisioned on a different system and shares removal_hours; kept separate because multiple capabilities on a check mean all are needed. 1Password marks people.leavers_deprovisioned n/a and points here. Related NEED password_manager: every shared vault has a named owner and members that match its team (IAM-05.C); no read only, complete API lists vault access, so no check is proposed.

checks.name: Changes are approved before release
checks.description: Every change ticket that reached its released status was approved first, by someone other than its requester and its implementer.
checks.remediation: Record the approval on the listed tickets, or raise each one released without approval as a finding.

controls.rationale: Shows each ticketed change was approved before release by someone independent of it. It does not show that every production change had a ticket, which tickets.changes_linked checks against the merged code.
Shows nobody approved a change they requested or carried out, for changes tracked in tickets. Other conflicting duties need their own review.

evidence_kinds: Change tickets with approval and release times

provider_notes.jira: Needs a status mapping (approved and released statuses, required impact, testing and rollback fields). Approval is a JSM approval, a transition into a mapped approved status, or a mapped approver field. JSM change management needs Premium or Enterprise; on lower plans approval is modelled with statuses or fields, which is weaker. Automation or app actors do not count as approvers (actor type field unverified).

checks.population: Change tickets in mapped projects that reached a released status in the last 30 days
checks.predicate: Approval before release, approver independent (account id differs from the reporter, the assignee at release and any mapped implementer), mapped required fields (impact, testing, rollback) not empty. The last approval before release counts; release is the first transition into a mapped released status
checks.period: Rolling 30 day window of tickets that changed state, checked daily; daily results are the Type 2 history
checks.empty_population: insufficient information: no released change tickets does not show no changes happened. Mapping not set or history truncated is insufficient

parameters.status_mapping: per project, which statuses mean approved and released, and which fields are required; set on the connection, audited, printed on every result

checks.notes: ticket in 1.4 needs approvals and status history (changelog author and time) added, or new types ticket.approval and ticket.change. Related, not an alias: tickets.changes_linked starts from merged code and looks for the ticket; this one starts from released change tickets. Fills change-requests-with-approval-for-a partially.

checks.name: Emergency changes are reviewed afterwards
checks.description: Every change released through the emergency route was reviewed and approved by someone else within the set window after release.
checks.remediation: Hold the missing reviews now and record them on the listed tickets.

controls.rationale: Shows each emergency change recorded in tickets had a review by another person within the window. Emergency changes made without a ticket are found by vcs.unreviewed_merges_recorded, and the authorization at the time stays with people.

provider_notes.jira: Needs an emergency marker mapped on the connection.

checks.population: Change tickets carrying the mapped emergency marker, released in the last 30 days, whose review window has closed
checks.predicate: A review approval by someone other than the implementer and requester, dated by the end of the next business day after release in the workspace time zone
checks.period: Rolling 30 day window of tickets that changed state, checked daily; daily results are the Type 2 history
checks.empty_population: pass only with an emergency marker mapped, and the result says emergency changes without tickets are vcs.unreviewed_merges_recorded; no marker mapped is insufficient

parameters.retrospective_review_window: SD-04 parameter; default the end of the next business day after release, in the workspace time zone
parameters.emergency_marker: mapping of the work type, field or label that marks an emergency change

checks.notes: Tickets still inside their window are listed as pending, not judged. Emergency changes made without a ticket are vcs.unreviewed_merges_recorded. SD-04.C (authorised at the time) stays with people.

checks.name: Access approvals are independent
checks.description: Every access request was approved by someone other than the requester and the person receiving the access, and each privileged request by an owner of the system.
checks.remediation: Have the system owner approve the listed requests, or remove the access granted on them.

controls.rationale: Shows no one approved their own access and that privileged requests were approved by a listed owner. That the grant matched the approved request is tickets.access_requests_approved.
Shows requesting and approving access sat with different people for tracked requests. Other conflicting duties need their own review.

evidence_kinds: Access requests with requester, beneficiary and approvers
System owner list used for privileged requests

provider_notes.jira: Needs JSM approvals or a mapped approver field, and a beneficiary field where requests are raised on someone's behalf. Independence uses account ids; emails may be hidden by profile setting (unverified).

checks.population: Access request tickets (mapped JSM request types or work types) approved or resolved in the last 30 days
checks.predicate: At least one approving decision from someone who is neither the requester nor the beneficiary; for request types marked privileged, an approver in the mapped system owner group
checks.period: Rolling 30 day window of tickets that changed state, checked daily; daily results are the Type 2 history
checks.empty_population: not stated in the connector document; the shared rule applies: insufficient information unless the provider shows the population really was empty

parameters.system_owner_group: group whose members may approve privileged requests
parameters.beneficiary_field: field naming the person who receives the access

checks.notes: Related, not an alias: tickets.access_requests_approved checks the grant matched an approved request; this one checks who approved.

checks.name: Security reports are answered in time
checks.description: Every report received through the tracked security channel had a first response within the stated time and a recorded decision when it closed.
checks.remediation: Answer the listed reports and record the triage decision on each.

controls.rationale: Shows reports that reached the tracker were answered within the stated time and closed with a decision. Reports sent anywhere else, and whether each incident reached the register, need other evidence.

evidence_kinds: Security report tickets with first response times

provider_notes.jira: Supported with a JSM first response SLA (needs an agent seat on the service desk). Partial on Jira without SLAs: the first public comment or transition by someone other than the reporter within the set time (read:comment:jira).

checks.population: Requests of the mapped security report types created in the last 30 days, plus any still open
checks.predicate: The mapped first response SLA has no breached cycle; without JSM, the first public comment or transition by someone other than the reporter came within the set time. Closed ones have a resolution
checks.period: Rolling 30 day window of tickets that changed state, checked daily; daily results are the Type 2 history
checks.empty_population: insufficient information; the dated nil return stays with people. No SLA or response rule mapped is insufficient

parameters.sla_names: JSM SLA names for first response and resolution

checks.notes: Feasibility matrix: S (JSM SLA), P (Jira without SLAs). ticket in 1.4 needs SLA cycles and first response fields.

checks.name: Ticketed incidents are in the register
checks.description: Every security incident raised in the ticketing system appears in Verity's incident register, or has a recorded decision there that it was not an incident.
checks.remediation: Add the listed incidents to the register, or record why each is not a security incident.

controls.rationale: Shows the incident register is complete against incidents raised in tickets. Severity, the notice decision and handling under the plan stay with people.
Shows each possible incident raised in tickets got a recorded decision. Whether the decision was right is reviewed by people.

evidence_kinds: Matching register entries and triage decisions

provider_notes.jira: Supported with the Verity register: an entry synced with source jira and the issue id, or linked by a person.

checks.population: Incident tickets (mapped JSM incident work type, or work types and labels) created in the period, filtered to security incidents by the mapped category
checks.predicate: Each has a Verity register entry (synced with source jira and the issue id, or linked by a person) or a recorded not an incident decision
checks.period: Rolling 30 day window of tickets that changed state, checked daily; daily results are the Type 2 history
checks.empty_population: insufficient information. Mapping not set is insufficient

parameters.incident_mapping: incident work types or labels and the security category

checks.notes: ALIAS: tests the same reconciliation as alerts.incidents_registered from a different source capability. Keep both keys while a check's capabilities all have to be connected (as checks.json treats them today): one merged key with ticketing and alerting would demand both Jira and PagerDuty. If the engine gains either of these capabilities, keep alerts.incidents_registered (incidents are its native object, machine recorded, and its empty rule is the sharper one) and add jira as an implementation. Conflict: this key's empty population is insufficient, the PagerDuty one passes when the list was read in full. Needs the verity_tasks register to hold a triage decision and expose completeness by source and external_id (operations owner decision 3, incident sync). Fills security-incident-register for completeness only.

checks.name: Someone is on call at all times
checks.description: For every in scope service, the first escalation level had someone on call for the whole period, with a second level behind it.
checks.remediation: Fill the listed gaps in the schedule and add a backup level to the policy.

controls.rationale: Shows someone, with a backup, was on call for every minute of the period on the in scope services. Contact details and whether cover meets customer commitments are reviewed by people.

evidence_kinds: On call entries per escalation level

provider_notes.pagerduty: On call entries from GET /oncalls per escalation level. A schedule type whose entries cannot be computed (v3 schedules, unverified) reads insufficient. Past rendering may change after edits (unverified); Verity's daily result is the record.
provider_notes.slack: Slack has no on call schedule.

checks.population: Escalation policies of in scope services (customer selected, all active services by default)
checks.predicate: For the last full day (UTC), the on call entries at level 1 cover every minute, and a level 2 with a different target also covers every minute
checks.period: Last full day (UTC), checked daily; the next 7 days are shown as a warning, not judged
checks.empty_population: not stated in the connector document; the shared rule applies
checks.notes: New observation types proposed: escalation_policy and on_call_entry (schedules and their coverage); none of the 1.4 types fits. Fills on-call-schedule FULL for LM-08.B over the period it ran (it is the schedule for the whole period); contact details stay with people.

checks.name: Unanswered pages escalate
checks.description: Every in scope service routes to an escalation policy that passes an unanswered page to another target within the set time.
checks.remediation: Add a second level, or shorten the escalation delay, on the listed policies.

controls.rationale: Shows the tool escalates an unanswered page to another person within the set time. Whether the settings match the approved escalation policy is a person's review.

evidence_kinds: Escalation policies with levels, targets and delays

provider_notes.pagerduty: Escalation policies with rules (delay, targets), loops and services. Audit Trail does not record escalation level changes, so Verity's daily snapshots are the change history.

checks.population: Escalation policies of in scope services
checks.predicate: At least two levels, each with a target; level 1 escalates within the set delay; level 2 targets someone other than level 1
checks.period: Point in time, checked daily
checks.empty_population: not stated in the connector document; the shared rule applies
checks.notes: New observation types proposed: escalation_policy and service (service to policy routing). escalation-policy is a document artifact (LM-08.A, C); the check fills only the configuration, approval of the policy stays with people.

checks.name: Paged incidents are in the register
checks.description: Every security or major incident in the on call tool appears in Verity's incident register, or has a recorded decision there that it was not a security incident.
checks.remediation: Add the listed incidents to the register, or record why each is not a security incident.

controls.rationale: Shows each paged security event got a recorded decision on whether it is an incident. Whether the decision was right is reviewed by people.
Shows the incident register is complete against security incidents paged in the period. Severity, the notice decision and handling under the plan stay with people.

evidence_kinds: Security and major incidents in the period
Matching register entries and triage decisions

provider_notes.pagerduty: Supported with the Verity register: an entry synced with source pagerduty and the incident id, or linked by a person. Historic data: Free 3 months, Professional 1 year.
provider_notes.slack: Slack has no incident record; incident channels hold conversation Verity does not read.

checks.population: Incidents in the last 30 days on services marked as security, plus any at or above the mapped major priority
checks.predicate: Each has a Verity register entry (synced with source pagerduty and the incident id, or linked by a person), or a recorded decision that it was not a security incident
checks.period: Last 30 days, checked daily
checks.empty_population: pass only when the incident list was read in full. Register sync off and nothing linked is insufficient

parameters.major_priority: the priority at or above which an incident counts as major
parameters.security_services: services the customer marks as carrying security alerts

checks.notes: ALIAS of tickets.incidents_registered (same reconciliation, alerting source). See that entry: keep both while capabilities are all required; if the engine allows either capability, keep this key and add jira as an implementation. Conflict: this key passes on an empty list read in full, the Jira key reads insufficient. Fills security-incident-register for completeness only, and sample-of-evaluated-events-with-the partially.

checks.name: Major incidents have a completed review
checks.description: Every major or high priority incident resolved in the period has a completed post incident review within the set number of days.
checks.remediation: Complete the review for the listed incidents.

controls.rationale: Shows each major incident got a completed review in time. The content of the review, and its actions tracked to closure, are checked by people and the Tasks module.

evidence_kinds: Post incident reviews with status and completion time

provider_notes.pagerduty: Post incident reviews need the Professional plan and above, and only count when the customer says reviews live in PagerDuty; a 402 reads not on plan and the artifact stays with people.

checks.population: Only when the customer says reviews live in PagerDuty: incidents at or above the major priority resolved between 14 and 44 days ago
checks.predicate: A review with status completed, completed within the set days of resolution
checks.period: Incidents resolved between 14 and 44 days ago, checked daily
checks.empty_population: not stated in the connector document; the shared rule applies
checks.notes: New observation type proposed: incident_review (status started, in review, completed; created; completed). Review content and its actions stay with people and the Tasks module (tickets.remediation_tracked with LM-05).

checks.name: High priority alerts page someone
checks.description: Every enabled high priority monitor or alert rule notifies an on call destination, not only email or chat.
checks.remediation: Add the paging tool as a destination on the listed monitors.

controls.rationale: Shows high priority alerts are sent to the paging tool. Whether someone is on call there is alerts.on_call_covered.
Shows each high priority alert has a destination that leads to a response. Tuning and removing unused alerts stay with people.

evidence_kinds: Monitors and alert rules with their notification targets

provider_notes.datadog: Monitors at or above the mapped priority (default 1 and 2) and Cloud SIEM rules with high or critical cases; on call handles @pagerduty-, @oncall- or a webhook the customer marks as paging. Draft monitors excluded. Opsgenie handle format unverified.
provider_notes.sentry: Enabled alerts on production projects marked high priority (default all with a production environment); an action targeting PagerDuty or Opsgenie (exact type values unverified) or a webhook marked as paging. Build only on the new workflows and detectors endpoints.

checks.population: Enabled high priority monitors and alert rules (Datadog: priority at or above the mapping and Cloud SIEM rules with high or critical cases; Sentry: alerts on production projects marked high priority)
checks.predicate: Each notification includes an on call destination (a paging tool handle or a webhook marked as paging); email or chat alone fails
checks.period: Point in time, checked daily
checks.empty_population: insufficient information: Datadog when no monitor has a priority and no tag mapping is set; Sentry when no alert is in the population

parameters.paging_handles: default @pagerduty- and @oncall-; webhooks the customer marks as paging

checks.notes: Also reads detection rules on Datadog (new observation type detection_rule). Fills on-call-schedule for LM-08.C (alerts reach the rotation) per datadog.md and sentry.md, and review-of-alert-tuning partially. Related: alerts.security_routed (routing on the paging side).

checks.name: Production services are monitored
checks.description: Every production service known to the monitoring tool has at least one enabled alert that notifies someone.
checks.remediation: Add an alert for each listed service.

controls.rationale: Shows no production service is left without an alert. Whether the alerts cover the priority conditions is reviewed by people.

provider_notes.datadog: Needs APM services in the mapped production environments, catalog entities with a production lifecycle, or production tagged hosts when APM is not used. Matching is a reading of queries and tags, shown per service.
provider_notes.sentry: Projects with a production environment; each needs an enabled monitor with at least one enabled alert that has an action.

checks.population: Production services known to the monitoring tool (Datadog APM services, production catalog entities and production tagged hosts; Sentry projects with a production environment)
checks.predicate: Each is matched by at least one enabled monitor or alert, referencing it by service or host scope, that notifies someone
checks.period: Point in time, checked daily
checks.empty_population: insufficient information when no production services are found (APM off and no tags, or no project with a production environment)
checks.notes: New observation type proposed: service (APM services, catalog entities, Sentry projects). Hosts disappear from Datadog after 7 days.

checks.name: A silent log source raises an alert
checks.description: Every in scope log source has an enabled alert that fires when the source stops sending.
checks.remediation: Add a missing data alert for each listed source.

controls.rationale: Shows a source that stops sending raises an alert. Whether every in scope system sends its logs is compared with the asset inventory by people.

provider_notes.datadog: Needs the list of in scope log sources (or an import from the asset inventory).

checks.population: In scope log sources the customer lists
checks.predicate: Each has an enabled log monitor on that source that alerts on missing data or a count below a threshold, notifying someone
checks.period: Point in time, checked daily
checks.empty_population: insufficient information when no sources are listed

parameters.log_sources: the in scope log sources, listed by the customer or taken from the asset inventory

checks.notes: New observation type proposed: log_source (customer listed sources). Sentry is n/a. Fills evidence-logs-are-reviewed for LM-02.B.

checks.name: Detection rules are on and notify
checks.description: Enabled detection rules cover each condition the alerting standard names, and every high or critical case notifies someone.
checks.remediation: Turn on a rule for each listed condition and add a notification to its high and critical cases.

controls.rationale: Shows enabled detection rules exist for each condition the alerting standard names and that serious cases notify someone. Tuning stays with people.
Shows security events are reviewed continuously by rules, which LM-02.D accepts in place of a daily human review. The monthly review record stays with people.
Where the cloud audit trail feeds the rules, shows control plane misuse is detected. Turning on the provider's own detection service is cloud.threat_detection.

evidence_kinds: Detection rules with state, cases and notifications
Mapping of rules to the conditions in the alerting standard

provider_notes.datadog: Cloud SIEM product only; without it the check reads not on plan once per connection. Rule to condition mapping proposed by Verity from rule names and tags, confirmed by the customer.

checks.population: Cloud SIEM rules not deleted, against the conditions the workspace's alerting standard names (LM-09.B list by default)
checks.predicate: Each condition has at least one enabled rule mapped to it; every enabled rule's high and critical cases notify someone
checks.period: Point in time, checked daily
checks.empty_population: not stated beyond not on plan without Cloud SIEM; the shared rule applies

parameters.conditions: the condition list in the alerting standard (LM-09.B by default)
parameters.rule_mapping: rules mapped to conditions, customer confirmed

checks.notes: New observation type proposed: detection_rule; none of the 1.4 types fits. Reads its condition list from the alerting standard (alerting-standard, a document; LM-09.B list by default), so that list must be machine readable. Fills evidence-logs-are-reviewed for LM-02.D. Related: cloud.threat_detection (NS-05).

checks.name: Security signals are triaged in time
checks.description: Every high or critical security signal was taken up by a named person within the response time, and every closed signal carries a reason.
checks.remediation: Triage the listed signals and record a reason on each one closed.

controls.rationale: Shows each serious security signal was looked at by a named person in time and closed with a reason. Whether it was an incident, and is in the register, stays with people.
For threat detection findings that reach the SIEM, shows each was triaged within the response time. Findings that never reach the SIEM need their own evidence.

evidence_kinds: Security signals with triage state, assignee and times

provider_notes.datadog: Cloud SIEM product only. decisions.question: Default thresholds the new checks use until the workspace's procedures set them: first response to a security report 2 business days, acknowledgement of a high urgency page 30 minutes, escalation delay 30 minutes, signal triage 24 hours, error triage 72 hours, post incident review within 14 days, HSTS lifetime 180 days, device key expiry 180 days. Each is a proposal, not a rule from a standard.
decisions.recommendation: Accept as proposals, overridden by the workspace procedure.

decisions.topic: HRIS breadth through a unified API
decisions.question: Buy HRIS breadth through a unified API vendor (Merge, Finch) as Drata and Secureframe do, or build each HR connector. A new dependency, needs an ADR.
Build an osquery based agent for teams with no MDM, or adopt Fleet (Go, MIT) as a base, with its code or query list public. An ADR decides build or adopt.

existing_check_changes.rationale: Lists high urgency pages that were not acknowledged in time. Reviewing them and fixing cover stay with people.
Shows postmortem actions tracked in tickets closed by their due date. Whether the actions fix the cause is reviewed by people.

Population gains postmortem actions (tickets the customer marks as findings or postmortem actions, open or closed in the period); the predicate also judges tickets closed late, since verity.tasks.remediation_in_sla judges open tasks only.
Add hr_system: every active employee needs a staff list; the vault alone cannot say who is missing.
Blocks some malformed requests at the edge. Validation inside the application is tested separately.
Predicate: name the exclusions. Every real tenant excludes break glass accounts; the check lists each exclusion and passes only when each has an approved exception (IAM-03.D).
Implement on Cloudflare only; Tailscale is WireGuard and has no TLS version setting.

NEED identity_provider: the identity provider behind the remote access tool requires a second factor for every member. Reuse idp.mfa_enforced joined on the members of the tailnet or Cloudflare Access, for NS-11.B and IAM-03.B (a mapping to NS-11 or a source on remote-access-settings-and-members; the document does not say which).

NEED cloud_infrastructure: each archive bucket that holds logs keeps them for the policy period (cloud.storage_lifecycle with a log bucket population), so observability.logs_retained can pass when retention relies on an archive (LM-02.C).
On Entra, a user's signInSessionsValidFromDateTime after the end date would show sessions were revoked, for IAM-11.D on removal-records-for-a-sample-of (readable with User.Read.All is unverified).

needs.need: identity_provider: the identity provider behind the remote access tool requires a second factor for every member (reuse idp.mfa_enforced joined on tailnet or Access members)
cloud_infrastructure: security groups or firewalls in front of each origin allow inbound web traffic only from the edge's published ranges, or no public port where a tunnel is used
cloud_infrastructure: each archive bucket that holds logs keeps them for the policy period (cloud.storage_lifecycle with a log bucket population)
verity_tasks: incidents imported from a connector land in the register with a triage decision field; the register exposes completeness against source and external_id
verity (notifications): a delivery log of security messages Verity sent (channel, time, provider message id)
business application: an export of the accounts holding admin roles in each tool, for the privileged access list
needs.raised_by: slack, sentry, datadog, pagerduty, jira, cloudflare, tailscale
